ai.title: Disable followup clicks after Freebuff session ends
ai.summary: SuggestFollowupsItem disables buttons when IS_FREEBUFF and session status is 'ended'. Uses useFreebuffSessionStore to track state. Prevents actions on dead sessions.

eli5.text: When you're using the Freebuff session in the CLI and that session ends, the follow-up suggestion buttons will now turn gray and stop responding to clicks. This prevents you from accidentally triggering actions on a session that's already closed. If you look at the follow-up buttons after your Freebuff session ends, you'll see they're disabled instead of being clickable as they were before.

ai.title: Fix CLI model picker showing false No wait after session ends
ai.summary: Freebuff CLI model picker now fetches queue depths immediately after a session ends to prevent flashing "No wait" on all rows. `use-freebuff-session.ts` initiates a fire-and-forget GET request in 'landing' mode, extracting only `queueDepthByModel` to avoid triggering silent auto-rejoins from stale server states. `freebuff-model-selector.tsx` returns null for ahead counts when depths are missing, keeping hints blank until data arrives. Scope: CLI hooks and components.

eli5.text: When a Freebuff session ends, the model picker briefly showed "No wait" on every row before refreshing the real queue lengths. Now, right after a session ends, the picker immediately fetches just the up-to-date queue lengths in the background, so you see the correct "N ahead" hints instead of the misleading "No wait" flash. The hint stays blank until the real numbers land, and live queue data is fetched as soon as you pick a model to join. This is live today for Freebuff session users.

ai.title: Freebuff version bumped to 0.0.45
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI package version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json was incremented from 0.0.44 to 0.0.45 as part of the release-bump commit 5ebfc491. This bump accompanies the same-day release updates including disabled followup clicks after session end (76c3d449) and a fix for false "No wait" flashes in the CLI model picker after session termination (938191c3). The version change grounds the 0.0.45 packaging milestone within the surrounding Freebuff monorepo release sequence.
ai.evidence: Commit 5ebfc491 modifies freebuff/cli/release/package.json, changing the version field from "0.0.44" to "0.0.45". This is a release-bump commit with +1/-1 stats in the Packaging area and Category.

ai.title: Hourly bot-sweep dry-run endpoint and admin scripts
ai.summary: Added /api/admin/bot-sweep endpoint triggered by hourly GitHub Action (.github/workflows/bot-sweep.yml). Uses shared secret auth (BOT_SWEEP_SECRET) and optional GitHub PAT (BOT_SWEEP_GITHUB_TOKEN) to identify abuse suspects via new abuse-detection/abuse-review logic in web/src/server/free-session/. Introduces FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS in common/src/constants/free-agents.ts to filter root orchestrator agents (base2-free) from subagents for accurate usage counting. Includes dry-run scripts (inspect-freebuff-active.ts, test-bot-sweep.ts) and unban utility (unban-freebuff-users.ts) for manual review.

eli5.text: Every hour, the system now automatically runs a quiet background check over free CodeBuff sessions and emails the team a report of accounts that look suspicious, like ones with too many shared devices or rapid-fire messages; no one gets banned automatically, the report is just for a human to review. If you're a free user whose activity pattern trips the heuristic, you won't be blocked right away, but your name could surface in that hourly email. The sweep only counts the main orchestrator agent for each session, so extra helper bots it spawns won't accidentally make you look more active than you really are.

ai.title: Session endpoints reject banned users
ai.summary: Added 'banned' terminal status to Freebuff session endpoints, returning HTTP 403 to prevent banned accounts from joining the queue. `resolveUser` now fetches the `banned` field; `requestSession` and `getSessionState` short-circuit if true. CLI `use-freebuff-session` treats 403 with `banned` body as terminal, stopping polling; `WaitingRoomScreen` displays an account unavailable message. Server `queueDepthsByModel` and `queuePositionFor` filter out banned users via SQL `NOT EXISTS` to stabilize queue counters.

eli5.text: If your account is banned, you'll now see a clear 'Account unavailable' message right away instead of spinning in the waiting room. The system now checks your account status when you try to join, so banned accounts are turned away at the door rather than quietly inflating the queue numbers. You won't be able to enter the queue at all, and the counter you see will no longer jump around when banned accounts are cleaned out.

ai.title: Adjust abuse scoring for established GitHub accounts
ai.summary: Added negative score adjustments in `abuse-detection.ts` for GitHub accounts aged ≥1 year (-20) and ≥3 years (-40). This acts as a counter-signal to prevent false positives on legitimate power users with old accounts. `abuse-review.ts` prompt updated to instruct reviewers not to tier established accounts as HIGH without independent signals.

eli5.text: The abuse-detection system now gives a score reduction to GitHub accounts that are at least 1 year old (-20 points) or 3 years old (-40 points), recognizing these as strong counter-signals that indicate a real, established person rather than a temporary bot account. This means a newly created account showing very heavy usage will no longer automatically be flagged as a high-tier threat if it's linked to an old, legitimate GitHub account. The review team was also given updated guidance on not over-flagging established users unless additional suspicious activity is independently detected.

ai.title: Add counter-signals to abuse detector
ai.summary: Abuse detector now computes agent diversity and max quiet gap hours to mitigate false positives. LAG() SQL queries track inter-message gaps and distinct agent counts in 24h windows. Review prompt instructs tiering down suspects with strong counter-signals like sleep gaps or diverse agent usage. Updates web/src/server/free-session/abuse-detection.ts and abuse-review.ts.

eli5.text: The system that watches for suspicious activity on free coding sessions now gives users the benefit of the doubt when their behavior looks human. Instead of only flagging red flags, it also looks for quiet gaps (like a 4+ hour break suggesting sleep) and diverse tool use (real users hop between bash, file picker, code reviewer, etc.; bot farms stick to one). When a suspected bot shows these signs, reviewers see the counter-evidence right alongside the flags and are told to lower their confidence. Live today for the internal team reviewing abuse cases.

ai.title: Move project picker before auth and waiting-room gates
ai.summary: Project picker rendering now precedes login modal and waiting-room checks in cli/src/app.tsx. Prevents auth failures or queue states from replacing the picker mid-flash, ensuring users select a working directory first. Affects CLI startup flow only. Logic relies on showProjectPicker flag evaluated before authentication state.

eli5.text: When you open the app and it asks you to pick a project folder, that screen now appears before anything else. Previously, a login screen or a 'please wait' queue could flash in and replace the folder picker, making it look like the app kicked you out. Now, even if your login fails or your session hits a queue, you'll always get to choose your working directory first, and only after that will the app prompt you to sign in or tell you to wait.

ai.title: Abuse review agent prompt tuning
ai.summary: Refined `abuse-review.ts` prompts to tighten bot detection heuristics. Counter-signal thresholds lowered (`quiet-gap` ≥3h, `diverse-agents` ≥5) while fresh-GH weighting increased. TIER 1 criteria clarified to require near-continuous activity (≥18h) or multi-signal stacks, reducing false positives on power users.

eli5.text: The system that watches for fake and abusive accounts is now better at telling the difference between a real busy developer and a bot. Instead of flagging heavy users just because they type fast, it pays closer attention to natural human habits: whether someone pauses for at least a few hours between sessions (bots usually don\'t sleep), whether they use a mix of different tools, and how long their linked accounts have existed. This means genuine power users are less likely to get mistakenly blocked, while accounts that act like bots around the clock (roughly 18+ hours of near-constant activity) or pair heavy usage with a brand-new linked account are more likely to be caught. ai.title: Add Carbon ad provider for CLI waiting room
ai.summary: CLI waiting room now queries Carbon (BuySellAds) instead of Gravity by passing provider: 'carbon' to useGravityAd. Server-side ad_providers/carbon.ts normalizes responses into the existing AdResponse shape. DB migration 0045_mean_sleeper.sql adds provider text column (default 'gravity') and extra_pixels text[] to ad_impression table, with payout now nullable. In-chat ads continue using Gravity as default.

eli5.text: When you open the CLI app and land in the waiting room before your first message, you'll now see ads from Carbon (BuySellAds) instead of Gravity, in-chat ads during conversations still show Gravity. Behind the scenes, a new provider switch passes 'carbon' to the ad-fetching logic, and a new adapter normalizes Carbon's response into the same format the app already understands. The database now records which network served each ad, stores any extra tracking pixels Carbon provides, and allows the payout field to be empty so it doesn't break when Carbon doesn't supply one. This change is live today for anyone who opens the CLI waiting room. Regular in-chat subscribers are unaffected, their ads come from Gravity just as before.

ai.title: Parse stringified tool-call input before Zod validation
ai.summary: Agent Runtime now attempts JSON.parse on stringified tool-call inputs before Zod validation in tool-stream-parser.ts. Malformed JSON from AI SDK repair failures previously bypassed validation, causing opaque errors. tool-executor.ts adds explicit stringInputError handling for remaining string inputs, returning actionable messages. Scope limited to packages/agent-runtime; no CLI/Web/Desktop changes.

eli5.text: When the AI assistant asks another tool to run, it sometimes sends the instructions as one long, messy text string instead of a neatly filled-out form. That confused the system and produced a vague error message instead of a helpful one. Now, the system first tries to tidy that string into the proper form before checking it; if it still can't, it tells you exactly what went wrong so you can fix it. This applies only to the background assistant runtime, not to anything you see in the app's menus or command line.

ai.title: CLI ads use ChoiceAdBanner for all variants
ai.summary: CLI chat and waiting-room screens now render all ads through ChoiceAdBanner, deleting the standalone AdBanner component. This unifies the ad UI and removes the manual disable button from the chat interface. The Carbon web provider was updated to fetch multiple ads concurrently to support the choice variant layout.

eli5.text: Starting today, the text ads shown while you're waiting for a response or while a model is thinking now all appear in the same clean banner layout used in the main chat, and the small "hide these ads" button that used to live inside the chat window is gone. For people using the free, ad-supported version (the Freebuff experience), ads may now show multiple promoted options at once instead of just one, because the system fetches several from the ad provider at the same time and picks the distinct ones. If you're not on the free tier, nothing about your ad experience changes today.

eli5.text: If you are using the CodeBuff CLI's free Chat mode and the service determines your location is not eligible, the session now ends cleanly with a clear country-blocked message instead of leaving you stuck waiting. The waiting room releases your spot immediately, and your chat window switches to show the blocked status with your country code, so you stop sending messages into a session that will no longer respond. This is already active for free mode users hitting the country restriction today.

ai.title: Refine quiet gap calculation in abuse detection
ai.summary: Updated `identifyBotSuspects` in `web/src/server/free-session/abuse-detection.ts` to calculate quiet gaps using window boundaries derived from user creation time and current time. The SQL query now constructs a `bounds` CTE to clip the observation window to `GREATEST(created_at, cutoff)`, ensuring leading and trailing gaps are counted correctly for fresh or recently active accounts. This change improves the accuracy of the 'user slept' counter-signal by including post-activity quiet time in the maximum gap calculation.

eli5.text: When the abuse-detection system looks at whether a user behaves like a bot, one signal it uses is how long the biggest quiet gap is in their activity over the past day (if you go hours without doing anything, that's a sign you're human, not a bot). Previously, the system only counted gaps between messages, so it might miss a long stretch of inactivity right after a user's account was created or right up to the current moment, especially for brand-new or recently-active users. Now, the system clips the time window to start from the later of the user's account creation time or 24 hours ago, and it also factors in the gap from the last message up to right now, so fresh accounts or users who just stopped being active get credited properly for that quiet time. ai.title: Region signal added to abuse scoring
ai.summary: Added heuristic region inference to `abuse-detection.ts` using CJK names, Chinese email providers, and `.edu.cn` domains. Score increases by 25-40 points only when combined with high message volume (`msgs24h >= 300/500`). Updated `abuse-review.ts` guidelines to treat this as corroborating evidence, not standalone ban grounds. Prevents false positives for diaspora users while targeting VPN-based farming clusters.

eli5.text: The system now quietly checks whether someone signing up for the free tier is likely outside the service's intended English-speaking and western-European audience, by looking at their display name (Chinese/Japanese/Korean characters) or email address (common Chinese providers like qq.com or.edu.cn schools). But it only treats that as a yellow flag when paired with very heavy usage, at least 300 messages in 24 hours, or 500 depending on context, and even then it only nudges the overall abuse score, which is meant as background evidence, not enough to ban someone by itself.
